item.title: This week's Tribune Obituaries PDF edition
Exuma man dies as airport lights fail
item.description: A WOMAN has revealed the heartbreaking tragedy behind her 76-year-old father’s death after an air ambulance sent to save him was unable to land in Exuma because the runway lights were reportedly not on, forcing the aircraft to return to New Providence without him on board.

item.title: ‘Price Pal’ app launches to increase transparency in the retail sector
item.description: THE government has launched a national price-comparison app that will allow Bahamians to check grocery and household prices across more than 230 stores in what officials say is an effort to increase transparency and competition in the retail sector.

item.title: Mother awarded $186k for childbirth tragedy at PMH
item.description: AN obstetrician and a medical office centre must pay more than $186,000 to a mother whose first child died during labour at PMH nearly 14 years ago, after a court found that critical steps to manage a known childbirth emergency were not taken and the baby was delivered without a heartbeat.

item.title: Bishop Fernander to step aside as president of BCC
item.description: BISHOP Delton Fernander will step aside as president of the Bahamas Christian Council this year, clearing the way for new leadership when the council holds elections in April.

item.title: BCA chief says lack of training fuelling surge in industrial accidents
item.description: THE head of the Bahamas Contractors Association (BCA) says a recent spike in industrial accidents highlights a troubling lack of on-site training, as labour officials echoed calls for more retraining across the sector.

item.title: New Bahamas price app will ‘cause more harm than good’
item.description: A Bahamian merchant yesterday warned that the Government’s newly-unveiled price transparency and competitiveness app will “cause more harm than good” for small retailers in its current format, adding that such operators should be “super worried”.

item.title: Foreign Affairs issues Middle East travel advisory amid escalating conflict
item.description: THE Ministry of Foreign Affairs has urged Bahamian nationals to avoid travel to parts of the Middle East following a major escalation in hostilities involving the United States, Israel and Iran.
